lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent:
Properties (props) make components flexible by allowing us to pass in data.

However, typing props.propName every time can get repetitive. There's a better way.

Make sure to pick props followed by props and then ., props, ..
lessons.hardModeContent:
Properties (props) make components flexible by allowing us to pass in data.

However, typing props.propName every time can get repetitive. There's a better way.

Use props for the parameter. Display each character in the heading and their catchphrase in the paragraph.

Make sure to pick props, followed by props, character, props, and finally phrase.

lessons.title: Intro - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Destructuring properties helps make code cleaner and more readable by directly extracting values passed to components.

Destructuring lets us extract properties directly from the function parameters instead of accessing props.propName.

Make sure to pick {, followed by character, phrase, and finally }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Destructuring properties helps make code cleaner and more readable by directly extracting values passed to components.

Destructuring lets us extract properties directly from the function parameters instead of accessing props.propName.

Use curly braces {} in the parameter to extract both property names used in the JSX.

Make sure to pick {, followed by character, phrase, and finally }.

lessons.interactiveContent:

Make sure to pick {, followed by }.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which syntax allows you to destructure props?

{ age, name }{props = age, name}[age, name](age, name)

{ age, name }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Destructuring props creates local variables from properties in a props object.

A component needs direct variables named age and name from its props object. Which parameter pattern creates them?

{ age, name }[age, name], which destructures an array.props = { age, name }, which replaces the props object.(age, name), which merely groups expressions.

Make sure to pick { age, name }.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the benefit of using destructuring in function parameters?

It makes the code cleaner and more readableIt slows down the performance of applicationsIt makes functions inaccessible from the browserIt is required for React to function correctly

It makes the code cleaner and more readable.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A component reads props.title and props.author several times. What changes if its parameter becomes { title, author }?

It can use title and author directly.It can no longer receive values from its parent.It converts the props values into state.It makes React require a class component.

It can use title and author directly.

PhonenameGadgetundefined

PhoneThe literal property name name.Gadget, the other displayed value.undefined, because destructuring removes props.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why is it beneficial to use destructuring with props in a React component?

It reduces the need to repeatedly write props.It hides props from the componentIt prevents reactivity in componentsIt requires less CPU usage

It reduces the need to repeatedly write props..
lessons.hardModeContent:
Why might a component destructure title and author from props at the parameter boundary?

It avoids repeatedly writing props. before each property.It stops the parent from passing those values.It makes the properties private to React.It turns both properties into state variables.

It avoids repeatedly writing props. before each property.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
When destructuring inside the function's arguments, which is the correct syntax for extracting name and price from props?

const Product = ({ name, price }) => {}const Product = ([ name, price ]) => {}const Product = <{name, price}> => {}const Product = ([ name, price ]) => {}

const Product = ({ name, price }) => {}.

When destructuring inside the function's arguments, which syntax extracts name and price from props?

const Product = ({ name, price }) => {}const Product = ([ name, price ]) => {}const Product = (name, price) => {}const Product = { name, price } => {}

const Product = ({ name, price }) => {}.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which of the following statements is true about destructuring props in a React component?

Destructuring reduces redundancy by allowing direct access to propertiesDestructuring is only for function bodiesDestructuring prevents passing props to componentsDestructuring can only be done in class components

Destructuring reduces redundancy by allowing direct access to properties.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A function parameter is { brand, model }. Which statement follows from that syntax?

The function can use brand and model without props..The component cannot receive any other props.The two values become array indexes.Only class components can use this parameter.

The function can use brand and model without props..

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the benefit of destructuring props in the component function arguments?

Allows for more concise and readable codeForces the use of class componentsPrevents components from accessing propsIncreases the file size of components

Allows for more concise and readable code.
lessons.hardModeContent:
What is the main effect of destructuring props in a component's argument list?

It gives concise local names for the needed prop values.It forces the component to use state.It prevents the component from receiving props.It changes a function component into a class.

It gives concise local names for the needed prop values.
